name: Poonthanam Illam (Keezhattur)
tagline: Ancestral house of Poonthanam Namboothiri — a Guruvayur-linked bhakti shrine and cultural centre
summary: Poonthanam Illam is the ancestral home of 16th‑century poet Poonthanam Namboothiri at Keezhattur near Perinthalmanna. It sits beside a small Krishna/Vishnu temple under Guruvayur Devaswom and…
description: Poonthanam Illam is the traditional house (illam) associated with Poonthanam Namboothiri, author of the devotional Jnanappana and a noted devotee of Guruvayurappan. The house stands in Keezhattur (Keezhattoor) near Perinthalmanna and is preserved as a cultural‑memorial site.

The property is maintained by the Guruvayur Devaswom and includes a small temple dedicated to Krishna/Vishnu adjacent to the illam, tying the site into the ritual and devotional world of Guruvayur. Local commemorations such as Poonthanam Dinam attract devotees from the region.

For visitors the Illam offers a compact glimpse of Kerala bhakti history: a simple traditional house, a memorial space and an active temple setting where temple calendars and astrology (prasna/Deva Prasnam) are part of how communities read and manage sacred life.

Because the Illam functions within a living temple network, visiting gives both literary and ritual context — the poet’s life, continuing Guruvayur patronage, and the local practice of temple divination and ritual consultation.
highlights: Birthplace and memorial house of Poonthanam Namboothiri (author of Jnanappana).
Adjacent Krishna/Vishnu temple maintained by Guruvayur Devaswom.
Active local festival day: Poonthanam Dinam (observed in Kumbham — Feb–Mar, Ashwathi nakshatra).
Site sits inside a living ritual network where Kerala-style prasna (Deva Prasnam/Ashtamangala) practices are used by temples.
Simple traditional Kerala illam architecture and a quiet rural setting near Perinthalmanna.

sections.heading: Background
body: Poonthanam Namboothiri (traditionally dated c.1547–1640) is one of Kerala’s best‑known bhakti poets; his Jnanappana remains widely recited. Local tradition places his birth and home at Keezhattur (also spelled Keezhattoor) near Perinthalmanna in Malappuram district. Today the Illam is under the care of the Guruvayur Devaswom, which maintains the house and the small temple beside it. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poonthanam_Nambudiri?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Walk the small memorial compound to see the traditional Kerala style illam and the adjoining temple dedicated to Krishna/Vishnu. The site emphasises devotion and literary memory rather than museum displays. Kerala Tourism and local guides describe the Illam as a cultural centre maintained for devotees and visitors. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/poonthanam-illam-kizhattoor-perinthalmanna/393/?utm_source=openai))

Time your visit to coincide with Poonthanam Dinam (observed locally in the month of Kumbham on the poet’s birth star, Ashwathi) for ceremonial readings and higher visitor activity. The Illam and the temple participate in annual observances that connect local devotion to Guruvayur practice. ([manoramaonline.com](https://www.manoramaonline.com/premium/life/2026/09/04/visiting-poonthanam-illam-the-birthplace-of-jnanappana-and-a-haven-of-peace-prm.amp.html?utm_source=openai))

If you are interested in Kerala ritual astrology, ask locally about temple prasna or Deva Prasnam events. Kerala’s prasna/Jyotisha traditions (including Ashtamangala/Deva Prasnam) are an established part of how major temples and smaller shrines diagnose ritual or administrative issues; Guruvayur and other Kerala temples have conducted such prasnams. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashtamangala_prasnam?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Reach Keezhattur from Perinthalmanna (the nearest commercial/town hub) by local road transport. The Illam is a short drive from Perinthalmanna; local buses and taxis serve the route. Confirm opening and visiting arrangements before you travel because the site functions within a temple timetable and Devaswom management. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/poonthanam-illam-kizhattoor-perinthalmanna/393/?utm_source=openai))

Respect temple etiquette: dress modestly, remove footwear where required, and ask permission before photographing rituals or priestly activity. If you want to witness a prasna or Deva Prasnam you should contact temple authorities in advance — such ceremonies are specialist, multi‑day events led by trained astrologers and ritual specialists. ([keralatempleguide.com](https://keralatempleguide.com/deva-prasnam-famous-cases-kerala-temples.html?utm_source=openai))

There are no large on‑site museum displays; treat the Illam visit as a short contemplative stop that pairs well with other Perinthalmanna area sites. Confirm event dates (especially Poonthanam Dinam in Kumbham) with local contacts or the Devaswom before planning travel.

latest.text: Travel feature on Poonthanam Illam highlights the site as a quiet spiritual retreat and notes Guruvayur Devaswom’s maintenance of the illam and adjacent temple.

Report on architect R.K. Ramesh, who had planned a cultural centre project for Poonthanam Illam, and note that the Illam and surrounding land are in Guruvayur Devaswom stewardship (takeover recorded in 1993).
Inauguration / opening of a Poonthanam Cultural Centre / memorial facilities at Keezhattoor is reported, marking enhanced local facilities for commemoration and literature events.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Cool, dry months and festival season — visit in winter (Nov–Feb) or during Poonthanam Dinam in Kumbham (Feb–Mar) for ceremonies.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Travel via Perinthalmanna (local buses/taxis to Keezhattur). The Illam lies in Keezhattur village near Perinthalmanna; check local bus schedules or hire a taxi from Perinthalmanna. For longer transfers use nearby railway stations (Angadippuram / Pattikkad region) and Calicut International Airport for air connections. Confirm local connections before travel.
etiquette: Confirm opening times and event dates with local Devaswom or village contacts before you go — the site follows temple timetables.
Dress modestly and follow temple etiquette; ask before photographing ceremonies or priests.
If you’re interested in prasna/Deva Prasnam, request advance permission — these are specialist ritual events led by certified astrologers.
Carry water and expect limited visitor facilities; combine the visit with a trip to Perinthalmanna for services.
